span.p: Is the target clearly and correctly defined?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Stop - fix the target definition; a fuzzy/leaking target makes every number meaningless

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Profiled shape, types, missingness, cardinality, distributions?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Profile first - plot distributions, not just summary stats the bimodal mean lies

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Any leakage candidates? cols absent at prediction time / target-derived / ID encoding the answer

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Flag them - exclude or defer to inside-the-fold; a suspiciously good signal is a leakage alarm

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Is the pattern exploratory or a confirmatory claim?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Route the significance question to applied-statistics - do not p-hack
